subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How many of the Five Ks are there, as symbols worn by initiated Sikhs?
questions.explain: The Five Ks are five articles of faith worn by members of the Khalsa.

questions.q: When the Khalsa was founded in 1699, the first initiated members were known as the:
questions.explain: The Panj Pyare, the Five Beloved Ones, were the first members initiated into the Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh.

questions.q: Which Guru compiled the first version of the Sikh scripture, the Adi Granth?
questions.explain: Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru, compiled the Adi Granth, the first version of the Sikh scripture.

questions.q: Which of the Five Ks is the steel bracelet worn on the wrist?
questions.explain: The kara is a steel bracelet, one of the Five Ks, symbolising the eternal nature of God.

questions.q: Why is sewa (selfless service) important in Sikhism?
options: It expresses love for God by serving others without reward
It earns money for the gurdwara
It is required only of the Gurus
It replaces the need to believe in God
questions.explain: Sewa expresses devotion to God through selfless service to others, performed without expecting reward.

questions.q: What does Sikhism teach happens to the soul after death until liberation?
options: It is reincarnated through the cycle of rebirth
It is judged once and rests forever
questions.explain: Sikhs believe in reincarnation, with the soul reborn until it achieves mukti (liberation) and unites with God.

questions.q: Sikh teaching strongly emphasises equality, including the equality of:
options: Men and women, and all people regardless of background
Only initiated members of the Khalsa
questions.explain: Sikhism teaches the equality of all people, including men and women, regardless of caste or background.

questions.q: Who was the first Guru and founder of Sikhism?
questions.explain: Guru Nanak was the first Guru and founder of the Sikh faith.

questions.q: What is the common Sikh name for God, meaning 'Wonderful Lord'?
questions.explain: Sikhs commonly refer to God as Waheguru, meaning the Wonderful Lord or Wonderful Teacher.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the Five Ks?
questions.explain: Kesh, meaning uncut hair, is one of the Five Ks worn by Sikhs.

questions.q: What does the Sikh concept of 'sewa' mean?
questions.explain: Sewa is selfless service performed for the benefit of others and the community.

questions.q: How many human Gurus were there in Sikhism?
questions.explain: There were ten human Gurus, beginning with Guru Nanak and ending with Guru Gobind Singh.

questions.q: The Mool Mantar, the opening statement of Sikh belief, begins with which words?
options: I take refuge in the Buddha
questions.explain: The Mool Mantar opens with Ik Onkar, declaring that there is one God.

questions.q: Who founded the Khalsa, the community of committed Sikhs?
questions.explain: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699.

questions.q: What is the Sikh holy scripture, regarded as the final and eternal Guru?
questions.explain: The Guru Granth Sahib is the Sikh holy scripture and is treated as the living, eternal Guru.

questions.q: Which of the Five Ks is the small wooden comb worn in the hair?
questions.explain: The kangha is a small wooden comb, one of the Five Ks, symbolising cleanliness and discipline.

questions.q: Which Guru declared that the scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib, would be the eternal Guru after him?
questions.explain: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Guru, declared the Guru Granth Sahib to be the final, eternal Guru.

questions.q: What is the 'langar' in Sikhism?
options: The free community kitchen serving meals to all
questions.explain: The langar is the free kitchen in the gurdwara that serves food to everyone equally.

questions.q: What is a Sikh place of worship called?
questions.explain: A gurdwara is the Sikh place of worship, housing the Guru Granth Sahib.

questions.q: Which festival celebrates the founding of the Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh?
questions.explain: Vaisakhi celebrates the formation of the Khalsa in 1699 and is a major Sikh festival.

questions.q: What is the Sikh term for liberation, when the soul unites with God and escapes rebirth?
questions.explain: Mukti is the Sikh term for liberation, when the soul is freed from rebirth and united with God.

questions.q: What does 'Ik Onkar' express in Sikh belief?
options: God has many forms to worship separately
questions.explain: Ik Onkar means 'There is one God', a core Sikh belief.
